description: I’m a first-year Master’s student in Data Engineering and AI, passionate about technology, space exploration, and innovation. I enjoy solving problems, sharing ideas, and collaborating with others. I’m looking for curious, motivated teammates with skills in programming, AI, data science, engineering, astronomy, research, or design. Creativity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn matter most. Let’s build something meaningful together!
summary: Welcome to Mazra’a! We built a decision-support tool powered by space data. Farmers face rising heat, unpredictable rain, water shortages, and tired soil, and choosing what to plant next has become a gamble. Mazra’a combines NASA Earth observations with local soil data, crop characteristics, and the farmer’s own priorities to compare crop rotation strategies that protect soil, save water, and build resilience. Meet Ghars, our chatbot, who talks with farmers in their own language, answers their questions, and explains every recommendation in plain terms. The farmer stays in control. Mazra’a gives farmers the eyes of a satellite, in their own language.
details:
Project Details

What it does and how it works

Mazra’a is a decision-support tool that helps farmers explore crop rotation strategies suited to changing conditions. It combines NASA Earth observations (such as rainfall, temperature, soil moisture, and vegetation health) with local soil information, crop characteristics, and the farmer’s own priorities, like saving water, protecting soil, or reducing risk. The farmer enters their field and goals, and Mazra’a compares rotation options and shows the trade-offs for each. Ghars, our chatbot, lets farmers ask questions and receive explanations in their own language, in plain terms.

Benefits

Clear, practical rotation guidance instead of guesswork

Better soil health and water conservation

Preparation for heat, erratic rainfall, and extreme weather

No technical or GIS skills needed

Intended impact

To give farmers, especially those usually left out of space-based data, the confidence to make long-term decisions that strengthen their soil, save water, and build resilience to climate change.

Creativity

Mazra’a turns satellite data into a conversation. Instead of charts and reports, farmers talk to Ghars in their own language and get answers they can act on. The farmer stays in control, setting the goals while the tool shows the options.

Factors we considered

Accessibility: language, simplicity, and low technical barriers

Local context: soil type, crop needs, and regional climate

Farmer priorities: different farmers value yield, water, or risk differently

Long-term resilience: rotations that protect the land beyond a single season

Trust and clarity: explaining why each recommendation is made
